title: A new church, a rate book
place: Vestry of St Dochdwy's Church, Llandough

cast.E_AGENT: the assistant overseer of the poor, Llandough parish
cast.B_JOHN: John Williams of Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr
cast.F_GWEN: Gwen, waiting to pay her own rate (fictional)

shots.direction: Date-and-place card over an establishing still. Spring morning, April 1872. The new St Dochdwy's Church stands on the inland hill at Llandough. It is six years old and its dressed stone is still pale and clean. The churchyard grass is short and wet, with older headstones leaning beyond the new walls. In the far distance, below the hill, are the Ely valley, the marshes and the grey line of the estuary. Slow push in towards the vestry door.

shots.direction: Still with a slow lateral move. On the churchyard path, John Williams (weathered, broad face, grey-flecked beard, dark wool coat and felt hat of the 1870s, heavy hands) walks towards the vestry door. Gwen (round face, rosy cheeks, silver curls under a bonnet, shawl over a print dress, reading glasses on a chain) follows a few steps behind with a small purse in her hand. Neither speaks. Birdsong and wind are heard.

shots.direction: Still with a slow push in. This is the vestry interior: a small, plain, whitewashed room with new pine panelling and a narrow lancet window. A hanging surplice is on a peg. The assistant overseer (pale, clean-shaven, thin-rimmed spectacles, dark frock coat) sits at a deal table. In front of him are a large open rate book, an inkstand, a steel pen, blotting paper and a leather document case. A wooden bench runs along the wall where parishioners wait their turn. Nothing in the book is readable.

lines.accent: Vale of Glamorgan Welsh (cy marked for native review)
lines.cy: Chwe blynedd ma'r eglwys 'ma'n sefyll, John, a fi'n dal i whilo am yr hen un. Wedi'i chario bant i Lecwydd a'i chodi 'to.
lines.en: Six years this church has stood, John, and I still look for the old one. Carted off to Leckwith and put up again.
lines.es: Hace seis años que está esta iglesia, John, y yo todavía busco la vieja. Se la llevaron a Leckwith y la levantaron de nuevo.

lines.accent: Vale of Glamorgan Welsh (cy marked for native review)
lines.cy: A nawr ma' tir y person yn mynd at ysgol. Ddydd Calan nethon nhw'i drosglwyddo, glywes i yn y swyddfa bost.
lines.en: And now the parson's land is going for a school. Signed over on New Year's Day, I heard at the post office.
lines.es: Y ahora las tierras del párroco van para una escuela. Las cedieron el día de Año Nuevo, me contaron en el correo.

shots.direction: The overseer looks up from the rate book, pen in hand, and addresses John across the table. His finger rests on a line of the ledger, which cannot be read. Medium shot on the overseer.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9, 1872 church vestry, a pale clean-shaven official in his fifties with thin-rimmed spectacles and a dark frock coat looks up from a large open ledger on a deal table, steel dip pen in hand, finger resting on an unreadable line, inkstand and leather document case beside him, grey window light on whitewashed wall, invented face, no legible text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Glamorgan Welsh, formal register (cy marked for native review)
lines.cy: Mr Williams? Goruchwyliwr cynorthwyol, at dreth y tlodion. Eich tro chi, os gwelwch yn dda.
lines.en: Mr Williams? Assistant overseer, for the poor rate. Your turn, if you please.
lines.es: ¿Señor Williams? Ayudante del inspector, por la tasa de pobres. Le toca a usted, por favor.

lines.accent: Glamorgan Welsh, formal register (cy marked for native review)
lines.cy: Rwy' wedi'ch cofnodi chi'n ddeiliad tir y llan yn y plwyf hwn. Y perchennog: y Parchedig H. H. Rickards. Ar y deiliad mae'r dreth yn disgyn.
lines.en: I have you entered as occupier of glebe land in this parish. Owner: the Reverend H. H. Rickards. The rate falls on the occupier.
lines.es: Lo tengo anotado como ocupante de tierras de la parroquia. Dueño: el reverendo H. H. Rickards. La tasa la paga el ocupante.

shots.direction: John stands at the table with his hat in his heavy hands. He answers dryly, half a smile in his beard, and puts a few coins down by the ledger. Medium close shot on John.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9, 1872 church vestry, a weathered Welsh farmer in his fifties with a broad face, grey-flecked beard and dark wool coat stands at a deal table holding a felt hat, wry half-smile, placing a few coins beside an open ledger, whitewashed wall behind, soft window light, invented face, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Vale of Glamorgan Welsh (cy marked for native review)
lines.cy: Felly fi'n ffarmo tir y person a thalu'r plwyf am y fraint. Sgrifennwch e'n deg, 'te, a fe dala i'n siâr fel pawb arall.
lines.en: So I farm the parson's land and pay the parish for the privilege. Write it fair, then, and I'll pay my share like everyone else.
lines.es: O sea que trabajo la tierra del párroco y le pago a la parroquia por el privilegio. Anótelo bien, entonces, y pago mi parte como todos.

shots.direction: The overseer dips his pen and writes the entry without looking up. He answers evenly, as an officer of the parish. Close shot on him, with the pen moving in the foreground.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9, close shot, 1872, a pale bespectacled official in a dark frock coat writing with a steel dip pen in a large ledger at a deal table, inkstand in foreground, calm neutral expression, whitewashed vestry wall, handwriting not legible, invented face, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Glamorgan Welsh, formal register (cy marked for native review)
lines.cy: Mae'r llyfr yn cofnodi pwy sy'n dal a phwy sy'n berchen, Mr Williams. Dyna'r cwbl mae e'n ei gofnodi.
lines.en: The book records who occupies and who owns, Mr Williams. That is all it records.
lines.es: El libro anota quién ocupa y quién es dueño, señor Williams. Nada más que eso.

shots.direction: Gwen rises from the bench with her purse ready as John steps aside. She speaks to the overseer with a little tartness. Medium shot on Gwen, with John at the edge of frame putting his hat on.
shots.image_prompt: photoreal 16:9, 1872 church vestry, a round-faced rosy-cheeked Welsh woman in her sixties with silver curls, bonnet, shawl and glasses on a chain rises from a wooden bench holding out a small purse with a brisk expression, a bearded farmer at frame edge putting on his felt hat, whitewashed walls, soft window light, invented faces, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Vale of Glamorgan Welsh (cy marked for native review)
lines.cy: A phan chi wedi bennu 'da fe, Mr Goruchwyliwr, ma' 'da fi'n un fach i'n hunan i dalu.
lines.en: And when you've finished with him, Mr Overseer, I've my own small one to pay.
lines.es: Y cuando termine con él, señor inspector, yo tengo la mía, chiquita, para pagar.

shots.direction: Closing still with a slow push in on the open rate book. The ink of the new entry is still wet and catches the window light. The coins lie beside it and the pen rests in the inkstand. The handwriting cannot be read. Only the vestry ambience is heard: a door latch and footsteps on the stone floor.
